blocking.issue: A task paused at the project's budget (and, by the same code, this month's cap) 'goes on by itself' immediately, without the limit changing. Every 30 s scheduler tick starts a new session that pauses again: an endless loop of sessions, withdrawn and refiled cards, urgent notifications and Updates.
blocking.evidence:
Root cause: a pause at an outer limit happens when the next call's worst case would reach 100% of the cap, which can leave the spend under the 80% finish line. caps.check with 1 µUSD then answers 'allow', so the wake fires right away.

Bench walk 4 (scratchpad walk4.cjs, steps 34-35), project budget CHF 0.01:
- The task paused having spent USD 0.0061 of USD 0.0125 (49%).
- Over the next 3.5 minutes, with nothing touched: 8 sessions (trigger 'message', one every ~30 s), each 'Stopped at the project's budget of CHF 0.01.'
- 7 cards withdrawn with outcome '"Write the guide for the project budget" goes on: its limit has room again.' plus 1 open.
- 17 urgent notifications (budget_stop and request_blocking alternating) and 8 Inbox Updates.
- The second session spent USD 0.002 more.
- Only cancelling the task stopped it.

With CHF 0.04 (paused at 90%) there was no loop.

The real API makes this likely: one call's worst case is USD 0.25-0.6 (16k output tokens), so a project budget of a few CHF can stop below 80%.

The only test (budget-pause.test.ts:473) calls wakeBudgetWaits directly, on a pause above the 80% line.

- SessionBudget.precheck takes an optional lineEstimateUsdMicro (default: the whole estimate). It fixes the run's line (wrapUpLineOf) and decides the wrap-up.
- The run cap, the session cap, its 80% and review-reserve lines (precheckCaps) and the outer caps still get the whole estimate.
- New read-only method SessionBudget.lineFor(runId, cap, firstCallUsdMicro, phase): the run's line, or the one its first call would fix.

enforcement/hooks.ts:
- EnforcementHooks.beforeModelCall(ctx, estimate, lineEstimate?) passes it on.

agent/loop.ts:
- Passes the tokens' worst case (priceAt(maxOut)) as the line estimate.
- Pays a call's searches only from the money below a work run's line: max_uses is at most floor((line - spent - tokensWorstCase) / searches(1)).
- Offers no new search once the wrap-up is due. A pending search still keeps the tool.
- Effect: before the wrap-up, a call's whole worst case stays below the line, and searches never eat the reserve kept to finish.

Docs:
- ADR 0107 point 4 amended ('With ADR 0112's wrap-up line', review of 2026-11-08).
- runtime.md (the wrap-up line and the loop), billing.md, user-guide (research: searching never eats the reserve).
